section.title: Introduction
section.p: BluetoothVoice provides asynchronous connection control and bidirectional PCM audio for a Bluetooth headset. This document is a draft interface proposal approved for implementation. The development module implements this contract for the native emulator transport: automatic discovery, HFP selection, security, CVSD voice setup and copied PCM playback/capture. It reports no endpoint while Windows owns the physical adapter. SWI and error numbers have not been publicly allocated.

section.title: Overview
section.p: A session connects one endpoint to playback and capture queues. A native backend uses BluetoothUSB and BluetoothCore for controller access and headset protocols. An emulator audio backend may provide host-managed endpoints using the same PCM interface. Applications identify the backend through capabilities and status; a host-managed endpoint does not imply native Bluetooth support.

An endpoint token identifies a device without exposing a memory pointer. A session handle identifies an open connection. Tokens and handles are opaque 32-bit values; applications must not persist them across module reloads.

subsection.title: Registers and memory ownership
subsection.p: R0 contains flags for every call. All flags are reserved and must be zero. Registers not listed as outputs are preserved on success. On error, the V flag is set and R0 points to a standard RISC OS error block. Registers other than R0 are preserved on error except for the documented Buffer Overflow result.

Input buffers are borrowed only for the duration of the SWI. Accepted PCM data is copied before return. Output buffers belong to the caller. No SWI retains a caller buffer pointer. Output structures contain little-endian 32-bit words and must be word-aligned.

Enumerate and Status support a size query with R2=0 and R3=0. They return the required byte count in R3 without consuming an enumeration item. A buffer that is too small returns Buffer Overflow and the negative required byte count in R3. No partial descriptor is written and the input cursor is preserved.

subsection.title: Version and capabilities
subsection.p: The draft ABI version is &00010000. Capability bits are: bit 0 playback, bit 1 capture, bit 2 native Bluetooth transport, bit 3 host-managed audio, bit 4 HSP gateway and bit 5 HFP gateway. Other bits are reserved. A capability is reported only when the backend implements it; it does not assert that every endpoint supports the capability.

subsection.title: Endpoint descriptor
subsection.p: The fixed descriptor is 96 bytes. Word offsets are: +0 structure size (96), +4 structure version (1), +8 endpoint token, +12 capabilities, +16 backend (1 native USB, 2 emulator host audio). Bytes +20 to +95 contain a zero-terminated UTF-8 display name, padded with zeros. A name is truncated only at a complete UTF-8 character boundary. Display names need not be unique.

Enumeration starts with cursor 0. A successful descriptor read returns its next cursor in R1; -1 means that descriptor was the last. An empty enumeration returns R1=-1 and R3=0 without writing a descriptor. A size query preserves R1 even for an empty enumeration; R3=0 indicates no item. Device changes may invalidate a cursor; restart enumeration on InvalidHandle. A descriptor token remains valid until the endpoint is removed or the module is reloaded.

subsection.title: Connection and microphone configuration
subsection.p: Connect accepts the original 16-byte configuration block: +0 size (16), +4 version (1), +8 profile (0 automatic, 1 HSP gateway, 2 HFP gateway, 3 host audio), +12 capture enable (0 disabled, 1 enabled). Other values are invalid. The module copies this block before return. Capture is disabled unless explicitly enabled here. A new connection is required to change this setting. Automatic selects a supported profile and reports the actual profile through Status.

Configuration version 2 is 64 bytes. Its first four words have the same meaning, with size 64 and version 2. Word +16 selects the discovered device: 0 chooses the first voice-capable result and 1 matches the Bluetooth address at bytes +24 to +29. The address uses HCI byte order. Word +20 is a PIN length from 0 to 16 and bytes +32 to +47 contain the copied legacy PIN. Bytes +30 and +31 and words +48 to +60 are reserved and must be zero. A zero-length PIN rejects a legacy PIN request. This configuration does not persist credentials.

Connect returns after queueing connection work. Status is polled until the session is ready or failed. A failed session remains queryable until closed. Read and Write before ready return NotReady. A removed device produces a disconnected state and DeviceRemoved on subsequent PCM operations.

subsection.title: Status descriptor and PCM
subsection.p: The status descriptor is 64 bytes. Word offsets are: +0 size (64), +4 version (1), +8 state, +12 backend, +16 profile, +20 sample rate in Hz, +24 encoding, +28 channels, +32 bytes per PCM frame, +36 queued playback frames, +40 queued capture frames, +44 playback underruns, +48 capture overruns, +52 last error code, +56 capture enabled, +60 diagnostic phases.

The diagnostic word contains four-bit session, controller, ACL link, ACL error, security, security error, voice and voice error values from least to most significant nibble. These values diagnose development hardware and are not stable application states; applications use the public state at +8.

States are 1 connecting, 2 negotiating, 3 ready, 4 disconnected, 5 failed and 6 closing. Before ready, PCM format fields are zero. Encoding 1 is signed 16-bit little-endian PCM. The first version exposes mono voice; sample rate is reported after negotiation. Applications must use the reported format rather than infer a rate from the selected profile. Queue counts use whole PCM frames; counter values saturate at &FFFFFFFF rather than wrap.
Development errors &Cxyy and &Dxyy identify ACL connection and security rejection respectively: xx is the component error class and yy is the raw HCI event status.

Read and Write accept byte counts that are whole multiples of the negotiated frame size. They never wait for hardware. Zero bytes transferred means an empty capture queue or full playback queue. Read with capture disabled returns CaptureDisabled. A zero-length PCM request permits a null buffer but still validates the session and its state. Module queues are bounded.

subsection.title: Closing and reset
subsection.p: Disconnect starts cancellation and moves the session to closing. Poll Status until state disconnected, then call Disconnect again to release the handle. Disconnect on a failed session starts the same ordered cleanup; release it with a second call after Status reports disconnected. Disconnect on an already disconnected session releases it immediately. Disconnect on a closing session is harmless. After release, use of the handle returns InvalidHandle. Device removal also retains a disconnected status until the caller releases the session.

Reset and module finalisation cancel outstanding I/O before releasing its buffers. Module removal returns Busy while a backend still owns outstanding transfers. The caller must close its sessions before application exit.

swi-definition.name: BluetoothVoice_Version
swi-definition.description: Reads the interface version and backend capabilities

use.p: Read this information before enumerating devices. Unavailable backends contribute no capabilities.

entry.register-use: Output buffer address, or 0 for size query

exit.register-use: Next cursor, preserved for size query
Required byte count, or 0 if no item

use.p: Returns the endpoint descriptor described in Technical Details. Buffer Overflow returns the negative required byte count in R3.

Allocates bounded session resources and starts connection work. Immediate validation or allocation failure returns an error and no session. Later connection failure is reported through Status. The first implementation permits one live session and returns Busy for another.

swi-definition.name: BluetoothVoice_Status
swi-definition.description: Reads session state and audio format

entry.register-use: Output buffer address, or 0 for size query

use.p: Returns the status descriptor described in Technical Details. Buffer Overflow returns the negative required byte count in R3.
Copies as many whole PCM frames as fit in the playback queue. The caller retains responsibility for bytes beyond the returned accepted count.
Copies available whole PCM frames and removes those frames from the capture queue. Capture must have been enabled at connection time.
Starts cancellation or releases a terminal session as described in Technical Details. It never waits for cancellation within the SWI.

section.title: Error Messages
section.p: Proposed symbolic errors are InvalidArgument, InvalidHandle, BackendUnavailable, UnsupportedProfile, UnsupportedFormat, AuthenticationFailed, ConnectionTimeout, DeviceRemoved, Busy, NoMemory, NotReady and CaptureDisabled. Numeric allocations remain pending. Buffer Overflow uses the standard RISC OS error. Queue backpressure is a successful zero or partial transfer, not an error.

section.title: Examples
section.p: Call Version, Enumerate and Connect. Poll Status until ready. Alternate Write and Read with normal application event processing. On shutdown, call Disconnect, poll Status until disconnected and call Disconnect again to release the handle. If connection fails, query Status for the failure and then release the session.

disclaimer.p: Development interface with unallocated SWI and error numbers; physical headset interoperability is not implied.
